items.title: Zach Cregger 表示，为了让持怀疑态度的 生化危机4：重制版 粉丝不把他当成“冒牌货”，他感觉自己就像在“…

content.v: https://i.17173cdn.com/gdthue/YWxqaGBf/kidhub/20260907/EyaecTbubBxpbAF.png
《生化危机4：重制版》导演 Zach Cregger 表示，在面对部分粉丝对他改编自卡普空恐怖系列游戏的电影所持的怀疑态度时，他感觉自己仿佛在进行一场“道歉之旅”。
生化危机4：重制版
动作, 恐怖, 生存恐怖, 第三人称射击, 僵尸
《生化危机4：重制版》很好地传达出了原作的神髓，与2、3代重制版不得不取消静态摄像视角相比，4代的原版将这个系列直接带到了新派游戏的起点上，因此相对应的，重制版需要更改的内容更少，但是它知道怎样将游戏打磨得更加现代化，它知道在哪里施加压力，什么时候让你呼吸，完美地平衡了生存、战斗和解谜，也完美地平衡了恐惧、兴奋和满足。现在我们只有一个问题：《生化危机5》，卡普空想好怎么重制了吗？
查看更多 立即下载
Cregger 曾执导过广受欢迎的恐怖片《野蛮人》（Barbarian）和《武器》（Weapons）。自从确认他的改编作品不会包含游戏中的任何角色，也不会讲述游戏中已有的任何故事以来，他就一直面临着《生化危机4：重制版》粉丝的审视。相反，Cregger 另辟蹊径，在《生化危机4：重制版》的世界观背景下讲述了一个恐怖故事，并引用了游戏中的一些经典元素。
在接受 The Playlist 采访时，Cregger 概述了在遭遇这种抵制的情况下宣传《生化危机4：重制版》的感受。
“我感觉自己仿佛在进行一场道歉之旅，”他说，“我感觉自己像是在竞选公职，试图让这些人不要叫我‘角色扮演者’（LARPer）。”

他在此处的言论与他最近在谈论《生化危机4：重制版》的反响时所表达的观点不谋而合。“我想我当时太天真了，”他说，“我原以为像我这样的游戏粉丝会因为有人站出来把《生化危机4：重制版》拍成一部生存恐怖电影而感到兴奋。我当时想，‘这太棒了。’我并没有真正意识到那种‘我们一直在等待里昂的故事’的情绪。我理解这一点，我很抱歉这并不是我要带来的故事。我明白，我理解这种挫败感。我非常理解，因为我没看过早期的《生化危机4：重制版》电影，因为它们看起来不像我所热爱的《生化危机4：重制版》，所以我怎么能对持有同样态度的粉丝感到不满呢？”
随着《生化危机4：重制版》上映仅剩一周，Cregger 对粉丝对电影的态度表现得很从容。“现在，我只想说，‘你知道吗？去看电影吧。’”他告诉 The Playlist，“如果你看完后仍然有同样的感觉，那么无论你认为什么都是公平的。由你来决定我是一个真正的《生化危机4：重制版》粉丝还是个冒牌货。我能说什么呢？我认为电影本身会证明一切。”
同样的，这些言论也呼应了他之前的观点。“我唯一的希望是，无论他们多么怀疑，或者因为我没有讲述那些游戏中表现得很好的故事而感到多么失望，他们都能去看这部电影。当他们观看电影时，他们会感到被理解，并能认出这部电影中对游戏的所有热爱，因为那确实存在，”他说。
“这并不是我随便讲个故事，然后贴上《生化危机4：重制版》的标签来骗取预算。而是在讲述一个《生化危机4：重制版》的故事。我理解这种抵触，我真的理解，因为我自己也有这种情绪。这源于真正的热爱。”
在接受 The Playlist 的同一次采访中，Cregger 表示他很乐意在《生化危机4：重制版》宇宙中讲述更多故事，但他也表示在《生化危机4：重制版》之后他将不再执导系列电影。
他会有机会制作另一部《生化危机4：重制版》吗？据 Deadline 报道，《生化危机4：重制版》首周末在北美票房预计将达到 3500 万美元，甚至可能更高。3500 万美元将创下《生化危机4：重制版》系列在北美最高的首周末票房纪录，超过了 2010 年《生化危机4：重制版: Afterlife》创下的 2660 万美元的开画纪录。

items.title: Do you ever listen to videogame music in your day-to-day life?
items.summary: Or should videogame music stay *inside* the game?

content.v: You know, I do a lot of prattling about videogame music at this humble website PC Gamer dot com. It's practically woven into the fabric of my very being at this point—hugely formative for me growing up, and now I carry little bits of it everywhere.

I have half a dozen VGM playlists dedicated to stuff like the gym, relaxing, and locking in at work. I've formed lifelong memories with friends as we've filled karaoke rooms with the sound of all kinds of Final Fantasy 14 tracks, where our so-called tastes in "regular" music might misalign; we're instead united by our mutual love and attachment to the songs we hear in a game.

In fact, it's so deeply entrenched into my everyday life that I can't imagine any videogame fan not listening to their favourite tunes outside of the game they came from. That is, until I was recently chatting with a friend where they told me just that: even if they really like a song in a videogame, they'll never go out of their way to listen to it detached from its origin.

So that had me wondering—how many of you actually listen to videogame music in your day-to-day life? Does it accompany you while you run errands? Do you have a playlist specifically dedicated to certain tasks or moods filled with songs from all of your favourite games? Or do you just get those random urges to listen to a videogame track that won't leave your head, leaving your YouTube or Spotify history littered with gaming-related earworms?

I'm interested to hear just how much you integrate videogame music into your day-to-day life, so be sure to drop a comment and let me know if you actually listen to any of it. And if you do, when or why are you doing it? I need to feel seen by my fellow sickos, please and thank you.

items.title: GSC Game World says there's a reason it didn't give Stalker 2 more time in the oven: 'To make something better, you need to receive feedback, and this feedback should be fresh'
items.summary: "Every developer would like to have an infinite amount of time, but … the market state is not very promising."

others.title: Guide: Every Nintendo Switch Online NES Game Ranked

content.v: Like a lot of survival games, Stalker 2 had a long journey from janky larva to playable, easily recommended butterfly. It's tempting to say that these games ought to just stay under wraps until they're done and relatively bug-free—but at Gamescom 2026, GSC Game World CEO and head of game direction Ievgen Grygorovych told PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens that deciding when to release is a more complex consideration than you might think.

As for why the studio didn't just wait to release the game until it was in the state it is now, Grygorovych cited both creative and financial reasons. "To make something better, you need to receive feedback, and this feedback should be fresh. From a business perspective, it's also impossible, because it's very expensive to do two years of additional work … in most cases, it's unrealistic."

GSC Game World has more legitimate reasons than most to release an unfinished game. The Ukrainian studio was working on Stalker 2 when development was interrupted by Russia's invasion , forcing the team to move out of Kyiv, and its progress was later hamstrung by a devastating office fire and numerous leaks . And notably, the game's buggy release did arrive after delays —but regardless of all the unique trouble GSC Game World encountered, Grygorovych pointed to woeful market conditions across the board as another consideration.

"You have to always find the trade-offs that allow you to bring the best experience you can with what you have," he said. "It's always a balance because every developer would like to have an infinite amount of time, but the market around is awful: lots of layoffs, studios are closing. So actually, the market state is not very promising. We're just trying to find the best configuration we can."

items.title: The Halloween game has a sex minigame in it, except no it doesn't, because it was apparently removed
items.summary: Some perverse pairings may be the culprit.

content.v: If you've seen any slasher flick, you know the drill: every youth is horny, and the horny must die. Despite Halloween not being quite as trope-riddled as some of its stabbiest contemporaries, its recent asymmetrical PvP adaptation did include a minigame where two players could slip into a closet and bang each other for buffs—but after only a few days in a deluxe edition-exclusive early access, the feature has reportedly been removed.

In fact, it seems to have been silently hotfixed out. The most recent patch notes make no mention of the sex minigame, but the comments sure do. On the Steam thread, one user commented "ADD BACK THE CLOSET MINIGAME" five times in a row. Others have noted that Lynda, a flirty playable civilian who previously got extra benefits from the sex minigame, has had that trait removed, which I can confirm with a quick launch of the game.

Players on social media are not pleased, as you might imagine. "Lame as hell," wrote Choice-Scholar-2297 on Reddit. A thread on the game's subreddit titled "Please add back sex mini game" is quickly gaining traction; freetheree's original post reads, "Why did they remove it!??!?!?!? Me and my homeboy just wanna have sex in a closet? And we can’t???? Tf??????"

Lots of the sorts of jokes you might expect are being thrown around, and of course, it is hilarious that if this change sticks the game will have had closet sex as an exclusive time-limited pre-order bonus. Unfortunately, there might be a good reason for its removal.

You see, players are also speculating about the reason this might have been changed: dead players can respawn as older characters, such as a police officer or Michael Myers' therapist Dr. Loomis. Fine on its own, disturbing when those characters can potentially solicit sex from a high schooler—Laurie Strode, for instance, is only 17 years old in the version this game depicts. While Illfonic has not confirmed this is why the feature was patched out, I struggle to imagine a more convincing reason.
I've reached out to Illfonic for comment on the patch, and this story will be updated if I hear back.
